title: uchar corpus case, format uchar-case-v0
description: One golden-corpus evaluation case: the input world, the evaluation date, parameter values, and the expected outcomes. Engine-neutral; consumed by the reference interpreter and any conforming backend harness. Values are unit-normalised to the referenced declaration's unit; numbers are exact decimal or rational lexemes carried as strings, never JSON floats.

asOfDate.description: The single evaluation date (valuation = calculation = vintage selection); null for a time-free case. The pattern checks the field widths, not the calendar: '2026-02-30' matches it. The calendar is checked one layer deeper, by each executor's case reader, which refuses a lexeme that names no day when it reads the case (red witness: corpus/rood/asofdate-kalender).

parameters.description: Parameter name (as declared) to value, in the parameter's declared unit. A granular parameter may carry its full timeline (the timeline variant).

expectedFault.description: The red-path alternative to `expected` (corpus/rood): LOADING OR evaluation of this case MUST fail observably in every executor that carries its form — never a silent skip, never a model. A refusal by the case READER is as valid a red outcome as a fault at evaluation: an ambiguous role key, a link to an undeclared label and their kin are the same observable refusal one phase earlier, and an executor reads this field on its own, before it builds the world, so a fragment can pin either phase. Each field is a substring the executor's fault report must contain: `ref` against the reference interpreter's fault, `clingo` against the ASP runner's fault or UNSAT report, and the OPTIONAL `drools` against the Drools backend's red-run fault report: a fault at fire, or a hard refusal while that run reads the case (a date lexeme that names no day). The `ref` and `clingo` fields are mandatory (both executors carry every red form). `drools` is present only where the v0 Drools backend carries the red-path form and faults on it; where it does not — a form the loader/transpiler refuses, or a constraint the backend does not enforce — gate 8's Drools leg lists the case with a reason instead. A case carries exactly one of `expected` / `expectedFault`.

label.description: Case-local instance name; unique within the case; the handle role links and expectations use.

attributes.description: Attribute name (as declared) to value, in the attribute's declared unit. Absence means empty (leeg); an input never carries an explicit empty. A temporal attribute carries either the asOfDate-bucket scalar or its full timeline (the timeline variant) — never both meanings at once.

roles.description: Role name (as declared) to the labels of the linked instances; a to-one role carries exactly one label.

characteristicTimelines.description: Full timelines of temporal characteristics: per declared temporal characteristic the true-periods, day-precision, from inclusive / to exclusive, ordered and non-overlapping, aligned to the declaration's granularity grid. Absence of a period means the characteristic does not hold there (a gap is clipped away, never leeg).

characteristics.description: Characteristics asserted true on input; every other characteristic starts false. A characteristic the IR declares TIME-DEPENDENT (a 'kenmerkGranulariteit' entry) is NOT delivered here — its truth is periods, and it belongs in 'characteristicTimelines'; every temporal reader consults that field and nothing else. This schema CANNOT enforce that: it validates the case document alone and never sees the IR's declarations, so which names are time-dependent is unknowable here. The three case readers therefore hold the rule themselves and refuse the static delivery at load, by name and with the reason (maintainer decision 2026-09-09); before that they accepted it and answered from an empty period set without a word.

value.description: A typed value; exactly one variant.

oneOf.description: A sum-type constructor value (CONSTRUCTS row 36): a declared constructor tag plus, for a unary constructor, its one payload value; 'payload' is absent for a nullary constructor.

A list value (CONSTRUCTS row 10): an ordered, possibly empty sequence of element values, all of the list's declared element datatype; the loader rejects a leeg element (spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.1).

A record value (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 11): the declared fields mapped to their values, each of the field's declared datatype. Filled by construction — the loader rejects a leeg field (the no-hole rule).

timelineValue.description: A full timeline: day-precision segments, from inclusive, to exclusive, ordered and non-overlapping, aligned to the declaration's granularity grid; absence between segments is a gap (leeg on read). The ref loader owns the cross-checks.

timeline.description: The expected full timeline of a temporal target, segment-exact (an empty array pins an empty timeline); ordering, non-overlap and grid alignment are the ref loader's cross-checks.

rule.description: Optional precision: at least one channel fact from THIS rule (name-normalised). Without it the expectation is satisfied by any channel fact, whichever rule produced it — precise pins close the false-green window where a case stays green on the wrong fact.

label.description: Optional further precision (requires rule): the flagged instance's label, exact. A created instance (no case label) never matches.
